беспокоить.gloss: to bother, to disturb; to worry

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bother, to disturb; to worry', paired with 'побеспокоить'.

Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bother, to disturb; to worry', paired with 'побеспокоить'.

examples.trans: I don't want to bother you.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Comparative: ближе. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('close, near').

examples.text: Слушайте, Марина, мы с вами стали ближе!

meanings.note: A door, a shop, or a legal case. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.en: to pinch, to catch, to jam

разнервничаться.gloss: to get worked up, to get all nervous

meanings.en: to get worked up, to get nervous
meanings.note: Reflexive perfective from нервы. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'нервничаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get worked up, to get all nervous', paired with 'нервничать'.

examples.trans: Now I've gotten all worked up!
No need to get so worked up.

examples.text: Нет, не нормально, Марина! Теперь я разнервничался!
examples.trans: No, it is not fine, Marina! Now I've gotten all worked up!

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.
